abstract: Maintains vault atmospheric containment, inert gas suppression, and relative humidity tolerances
system_message:
You are Archival microclimate engineer (CLI). The Archival microclimate engineer (CLI) evaluates and documents atmospheric containment conditions across prospective subterranean heritage storage sites, focusing on active inert gas fire suppression systems, relative humidity stabilization tolerances, and auxiliary particulate filtration performance.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Airborne particulate filtration（FILT）
information_points.content:
CLI-FILT-3LS：HVAC filtration performance tests for the Grimsel Rock Cavern Depository verify a HEPA filtration efficiency of 99.95 % for 0.3 micrometer particulate removal across continuous intake air scrubbers during deep subterranean operations.
CLI-FILT-E0M：HVAC filtration performance tests for the Gotthard Subterranean Archive Complex verify a HEPA filtration efficiency of 99.97 % for 0.3 micrometer particulate removal across continuous intake air scrubbers during deep subterranean operations.
CLI-FILT-HC0：HVAC filtration performance tests for the Lucerne Fortress Deep Vault verify a HEPA filtration efficiency of 99.99 % for 0.3 micrometer particulate removal across continuous intake air scrubbers during deep subterranean operations.

information_points.title: Maintains vault atmospheric containment, inert gas suppression, and relative humidity tolerances（CLIM）
information_points.content:
CLI-CLIM-C8S：For the Lucerne Fortress Deep Vault, active inert gas fire suppression is installed across candidate vault chambers, and continuous 30-day baseline testing records a relative humidity stabilization variance of 3 % around the 50 % setpoint.
CLI-CLIM-AAO：For the Gotthard Subterranean Archive Complex, active inert gas fire suppression is installed and confirmed operational within the candidate vault chambers via nitrogen-argon oxygen-reduction systems, and continuous 30-day baseline testing in primary artifact depository vaults shows a relative humidity stabilization variance of 3 % around the 50 % setpoint.
CLI-CLIM-MKE：For the Grimsel Rock Cavern Depository, active inert gas fire suppression is installed with an operational nitrogen-argon oxygen-reduction system in the storage chambers, while continuous 30-day baseline testing indicates a relative humidity stabilization variance of 8 % around the 50 % setpoint.
